sources: https://www.sfwmd.gov/sites/default/files/SUL_FAQs_1-30-20.pdf (the FAQ linked from the SUL page)

fees.source: https://www.sfwmd.gov/community-residents/recreation/sul ('Special Use Licenses can be obtained at no cost. A Special Use License or 'SUL' allows the public to engage in various recreational activities including camping, equestrian camping, camping with a RV or Travel Trailer'), read 2026-10-21

hookups.source: https://www.sfwmd.gov/sites/default/files/SUL_FAQs_1-30-20.pdf ('Do any of these campsites have electric or water hook ups? There are no campsites that have any electric or water hook ups.'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: RV/travel-trailer camping is allowed here (one of five SFWMD sites that allow it); the District sets no length limit.

sites.source: https://www.sfwmd.gov/sites/default/files/SUL_FAQs_1-30-20.pdf ('RV/Travel Trailer camping is limited to the DuPuis Equestrian Campground, The Istokpoga Canal Boat Ramp Area Campground, ...'; 'Is there a length limit for RV/Travel Trailers? There is no length limit.'), read 2026-10-21

facilities.source: https://www.sfwmd.gov/sites/default/files/SUL_FAQs_1-30-20.pdf ('The DuPuis Equestrian Campground is the only dump station available on South Florida Water Management District campsites') + https://www.sfwmd.gov/recreation-site/kissimmee-river-public-use-area-istokpoga-canal-boat-ramp-area (activities list includes 'Restrooms', 'Camping (RV/Travel Trailer)'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: A free SFWMD Special Use License, obtained in advance online, is required; the gate combination is printed on the license. Licenses for June 1-December 31, 2026 are open; popular sites open 4-6 months ahead. Up to 8 consecutive days per permit, then leave for at least a day; 30 days a year District-wide.

booking.source: https://www.sfwmd.gov/community-residents/recreation/sul ('Special Use Licenses for June 1-December 31, 2026 are now open') + https://www.sfwmd.gov/sites/default/files/SUL_FAQs_1-30-20.pdf ('Campers are permitted up to 8 consecutive days per permit. You must depart on the 8th day', 'There is a limit of 30 days per year, District-wide', 'Our more popular campsites are open for booking 4 to 6 months in advance', gate combination 'located on the bottom of the Special Use License'), read 2026-10-21

note: SFWMD gated campground in the Kissimmee River Public Use Area, on the Istokpoga Canal near Lorida, next to the Hickory Hammock trailhead. ~12 lightly-graveled drive-in sites plus ~6 spots in the treeline; tents or any size RV (Big Rig Friendly). Each site has table, fire ring, grill; restrooms. The Dyrt 4.5/5 (6 reviews). --Claude
summary: SFWMD pages + the SUL FAQ they link: confirmed free (SUL at no cost), RV camping allowed with no length limit, reservation by license. Added no hookups, no dump station, operator platform, 7-night max (8 consecutive days per permit). Not stated: site count, potable water/showers (derived values left). Note cleaned of the SUL/fee/max-stay/no-showers text the fields now carry.
flags: The FAQ used for hookups, length and stay limits is dated 2020 (SUL_FAQs_1-30-20.pdf) though still linked from the current SUL page.
